quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you are driving through an intersection.
When you are passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When you are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You may turn right after you stop completely.
You cannot turn right.
You can turn left.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows laws drivers must follow. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How much lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The full lane width, just like other vehicles.
Half a lane.
The sidewalk width.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full lane width, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are allowed to use the full width of a lane, the same as any other vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
One-way traffic is ahead.
Two-way traffic is ahead.
Stay on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the right side.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay on the right side of the divider ahead.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
You may see more pedestrians ahead.
The reduced speed zone is over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone is over.
questions.explanation: This sign marks the end of a school zone where the lower speed limit was in effect. You can now drive faster.

questions.question: A bus is signaling to pull back onto the main road after stopping. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Let the bus merge in safely.
Speed up to pass the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the bus merge in safely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to buses that are pulling back onto the main road. You can change lanes, slow down, or stop to help the bus merge safely.

questions.question: A traffic light shows a green arrow and a red light. What does this mean?

options.text: You may only go straight.
You may only go in the direction the arrow points.
Wait for a solid green light before you go.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only go in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can only drive in that direction if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You are driving uphill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass safely.
You may not be able to pass legally.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit on hills. It may be unsafe and illegal to pass on a hill where you cannot see ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is coming.
Several curves are coming.
An S-curve is coming.
The road is slippery when it is wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when it is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes very slippery when wet.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before you enter any crosswalk.
Stop before you enter the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before any crosswalk.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Only stop signs have an octagon shape. This eight-sided sign tells drivers to stop completely before going forward.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway:

options.text: As long as you aren't driving.
If you are riding in the back seat.
If you are riding in the back of a pick-up truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drink or carry open alcohol while on a public road or sidewalk. You also cannot keep an open alcohol bottle in the front or back seat of a vehicle.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus has flashing red lights and is picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, cars moving in both directions must stop while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must stay within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach the tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can listen for a train.
Only continue if a flagger tells you it is safe to do so.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Make sure no train is coming from either direction before crossing. Reduce noise so you can hear a train. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: A good rule to remember for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
Try to get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the risk of a crash. Driving faster than traffic means passing more often. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: Your chances of being in a collision increase after consuming:

options.text: Four alcoholic drinks.
Three alcoholic drinks.
Two alcoholic drinks.
One alcoholic drink.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink.
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink increases your crash risk. No one can drink and drive safely, no matter how much driving experience they have.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?

options.text: Yes.
No.
If there is no oncoming traffic.
If the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed. You cannot cross these lines unless you are turning into a driveway or business entrance. Passing over a solid yellow line is never allowed.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who might not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.
Do not follow specific rules of the road.
Are nothing to worry about.
Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Drivers must respect the rights of bicyclists on the road.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Demand the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give oncoming vehicles at least half of the road space. Both drivers need enough room to pass safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of a hazard. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: Only the driver needs to wear one.
Passengers should wear them on long drives.
All passengers should wear them on expressways.
All occupants should wear them every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants should wear them every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt every time. In a crash, an unbelted person becomes a flying object and can injure others.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, keep watching the road. Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly. Pull off the road when safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic signals, yield to the vehicle coming from your right.
